lists.name: Planet Hulk

lists.name: Greg Pak's Hulk: Planet Hulk to Totally Awesome Hulk

lists.name: Annihilation

lists.name: X-Men: Divided We Stand
lists.description: After Messiah Complex, the X-Men line divides, and Cable, X-Force, Cyclops and Wolverine each go their own way in 2008. Ed Brubaker's Uncanny X-Men opens the journey, followed by X-Men Legacy, X-Factor, X-Force, Wolverine, Cable and Young X-Men.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Secret Invasion: Main Series and Branded Tie-Ins

lists.name: Vision
lists.description: Vision stands with the Avengers from 1968 on, and his story keeps returning to the Scarlet Witch. Roy Thomas's Avengers opens the journey, followed by Vision and the Scarlet Witch and the West Coast Avengers, then Avengers No Road Home and Al Ewing's Avengers Inc. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Emma Frost
lists.description: Emma Frost first appears as the White Queen, and her story carries her to Generation X, the X-Men and Krakoa. Chris Claremont's Uncanny X-Men and New Mutants come first, then Generation X, Grant Morrison's New X-Men, Karl Bollers's Emma Frost and Joss Whedon's Astonishing X-Men. Immortal X-Men, Invincible Iron Man and Gerry Duggan's X-Men close it. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Doctor Octopus / Otto Octavius
lists.description: Otto Octavius, better known as Doctor Octopus, has been one of Spider-Man's oldest enemies since the early 1960s. Amazing Fantasy opens the selection before Stan Lee's Amazing Spider-Man, followed by Spectacular Spider-Man and Web of Spider-Man. Superior Octopus and Christos Gage's Superior Spider-Man come late. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Shang-Chi / Master of Kung Fu
lists.description: Shang-Chi, the Master of Kung Fu, comes out of 1970s martial-arts and spy comics and later headlines stories of the Ten Rings. Master of Kung Fu, mostly credited to Doug Moench, and Deadly Hands of Kung Fu come first. Heroes for Hire, Secret Avengers, Avengers World and Greg Pak's Agents of Atlas follow before Gene Yang's Shang-Chi series. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Thunderbolts
lists.description: The Thunderbolts keep changing shape, and Songbird, Hawkeye, Luke Cage and Red Hulk all turn up across their lineups. Kurt Busiek's Thunderbolts opens the journey, with later stories credited to Fabian Nicieza, Warren Ellis, Christos Gage, Jeff Parker, Charles Soule and Jim Zub. Matthew Rosenberg's King in Black: Thunderbolts closes it.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Namor (Sub-Mariner)
lists.description: Namor, the Sub-Mariner and prince of Atlantis, appears here from 1941 on, standing with the Invaders and the Defenders along the way. It begins in Sub-Mariner Comics, meets the 1960s Fantastic Four and Avengers, and runs through Roy Thomas's Sub-Mariner and Invaders. Chip Zdarsky's Invaders and Christopher Cantwell's Namor: Conquered Shores come late. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Nebula
lists.description: Nebula enters this story in the Avengers of 1985, and from there she is never far from Thanos, Gamora or the Silver Surfer. Roger Stern's Avengers opens it, followed by Jim Starlin's Silver Surfer and Infinity Gauntlet and Ron Marz's Silver Surfer. Jeff Lemire's Thanos, Cullen Bunn's Asgardians of the Galaxy and Vita Ayala's Nebula come later.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Hawkeye (Clint Barton and Kate Bishop)
lists.description: Clint Barton and Kate Bishop both answer to Hawkeye, on teams from the Avengers to the West Coast Avengers and in books of their own. It starts in Tales of Suspense and the 1960s Avengers, spends years in the West Coast Avengers, and later takes in Kelly Thompson's West Coast Avengers (2018). Matthew Rosenberg's Hawkeye: Freefall (2020) comes near the end, and Thunderbolts (2023) closes it.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: MCU Prep: Iron Man (2008)
lists.description: Read Iron Monger and Armor Wars to understand Tony Stark's fight to keep his technology out of the wrong hands. Obadiah Stane's campaign against Tony gives context to the film's armored rival, while Armor Wars explores the consequences of stolen designs. These are battles over Tony's legacy, not a retelling of his origin.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: The Incredible Hulk (2008)
lists.description: Explore Bruce Banner's origins and life on the run to understand the man, monster and relationships behind The Incredible Hulk. Hulk: Gray revisits his early days and bond with Betty Ross, while Return of the Monster follows a hunted Banner. These comics explore the tension the film draws on rather than its exact events.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Iron Man 2 (2010)
lists.description: Explore Tony Stark's vulnerabilities and meet Whiplash, Black Widow and War Machine in comics that add context to Iron Man 2. Demon in a Bottle tests Tony beyond the armor, Deadly Origin explores Natasha's past, and the War Machine issues develop Rhodey's armored role. Iron Man vs. Whiplash offers a comics take on the villain rather than the film's exact story.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Thor (2011)
lists.description: Meet Thor and Loki in the comics to understand the family rivalry and questions of worthiness behind Thor's first film. Season One revisits Thor's beginnings, Blood Brothers gives Loki's perspective, and the early Simonson issues introduce Beta Ray Bill, another wielder of Thor's power. Bill broadens the mythology rather than appearing in the film.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Captain America: The First Avenger (2011)
lists.description: Read First Vengeance, the film's comics prelude, to meet the people who shape Steve Rogers' path to becoming Captain America. These four chapters add background to the allies, enemies and wartime experiences surrounding the First Avenger.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: The Avengers (2012)
lists.description: Explore how the Avengers come together in the comics to understand the uneasy teamwork behind their first film. Season One revisits their beginnings, the Kree/Skrull War tests them on a cosmic scale, and Disassembled shows how fragile their unity can be. These later crises broaden the team's background rather than retelling the film.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Iron Man 3 (2013)
lists.description: Read Extremis to understand the dangerous technology adapted for Iron Man 3 and the questions it raises about Tony Stark. Enter the Mandarin introduces a very different version of his enemy, while The Five Nightmares and Stark Disassembled test Tony's inventions, identity and resilience. The film reshapes these ideas rather than following every comics plot.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Thor: The Dark World (2013)
lists.description: Meet Malekith and the Dark Elves in Thor's comics to understand the enemies brought to the screen in The Dark World. First Thunder revisits Thor's early days on Earth, then the opening Simonson run introduces Beta Ray Bill and Malekith's threat. The reading expands Asgard's mythology rather than retelling the film's Aether story.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Captain America: The Winter Soldier (2014)
lists.description: A mysterious assassin called the Winter Soldier emerges in the comics storyline behind the film. Man Out of Time first explores Steve Rogers' adjustment to the present, then the Winter Soldier arc turns that assassin into a personal crisis for Steve. Expect a different conspiracy from the film's.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015)
lists.description: Explore Ultron's comics history to understand the Avengers' mechanical enemy beyond the film's version. The Origin introduces the team, while Ultron Unbound and Rage of Ultron explore the robot's ties to Hank Pym and Vision. Age of Ultron supplies the film's title, not the same plot.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Ant-Man (2015)
lists.description: Get to know Scott Lang's second-chance heroics and the Ant-Man legacy behind the film's shrinking suit. Hank Pym and Janet van Dyne's beginnings lead into Scott's struggles with work, crime and fatherhood. The Irredeemable Ant-Man introduces a different suit-wearer, Eric O'Grady, rather than another Scott Lang adventure.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Captain America: Civil War (2016)
lists.description: Read Civil War to understand the comics' clash over superhero registration behind the film's divided Avengers. Captain America's surrounding issues follow the build-up, Steve Rogers' resistance and the conflict's aftermath. The comics involve a much wider superhero community than the film.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Thor: Ragnarok (2017)
lists.description: Read Ragnarok and Planet Hulk to explore the comics behind the film's Asgardian apocalypse and gladiator world. Earlier Thor adventures establish his mythic world before Ragnarok confronts its destruction. Planet Hulk follows Hulk on Sakaar, a story the film reshapes around Thor rather than adapting unchanged.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Black Panther (2018)
lists.description: Explore T'Challa's rule and Killmonger's rebellion to understand the struggle over Wakanda at the heart of Black Panther. Who Is the Black Panther? introduces the king and his nation, while Panther's Rage pits him against Killmonger. Later runs deepen Wakanda's politics and the tensions between royal duty and responsibility to its people.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Avengers: Infinity War (2018) & Avengers: Endgame
lists.description: Follow Thanos and the Infinity Gauntlet to understand the comics behind the films' universe-threatening stakes. Thanos Rising and The Thanos Quest trace his past and pursuit of the gems before Infinity Gauntlet brings the heroes together against him. Infinity War follows with a different conflict, not a retelling of the film.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Captain Marvel (2019)
lists.description: Explore Carol Danvers as Captain Marvel and the Kree-Skrull conflict for background on the film's hero and warring empires. The Avengers' Kree/Skrull War introduces the cosmic struggle, while Carol's later space adventures show her leadership and independence. These are comics counterparts, not a retelling of her MCU origin.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Doctor Strange (2016)
lists.description: Explore Doctor Strange's origins and life as a sorcerer to understand the magical responsibilities behind the film's hero. Season One introduces his beginnings, while The Oath tests his duties as a doctor and protector. The Way of the Weird, The Last Days of Magic and What Is It That Disturbs You, Stephen? explore the cost of defending a magical world.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: Doctor Strange: Multiverse of Madness
lists.description: Doctor Strange's magical New York gives way to the Illuminati, Marvel's biggest egos meeting in secret to keep the world under control. Jason Aaron's Doctor Strange comes first, then the earlier Illuminati special, the miniseries Bendis wrote with Brian Reed, and New Avengers. Heavy themes, big magic, and secrets that never stay buried for long.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Spider-Man: No Way Home
lists.description: Swing through Peter's tangled past, a desperate fight to protect the people he loves, and a brush with Doctor Strange's magic. Nostalgia, heartbreak, and magical trouble, all in one web.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Marvel What If?
lists.description: Alternate realities send Doctor Doom, Thor, Daredevil, Spider-Man and Magik down different roads, one story at a time. Stories from the original What If? come first, with Frank Miller among their credited writers, followed by later What If?, Age of Ultron and Magik selections.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: WandaVision
lists.description: The Scarlet Witch and the Vision share the spotlight across almost fifty years of comics, the history behind WandaVision. The journey runs from 1970s Avengers and Giant-Size Avengers through Vision and the Scarlet Witch, the West Coast Avengers and the Scarlet Witch's solo series, then to later Avengers and No Road Home, and closes with House of X and Empyre: X-Men.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Spider-Man: Far From Home
lists.description: Mysterio, the Gauntlet and Peter Parker's neighborhood stakes tie these Spider-Man stories to Far From Home. The selection moves from Stan Lee's Amazing Spider-Man to Roger Stern's Spectacular Spider-Man, Dan Slott's Amazing Spider-Man and Tom Taylor's Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
lists.description: Explore Shang-Chi's family legacy in modern comics for context on the film's conflict between duty and independence. Agents of Atlas and Sword Master introduce allies before Shang-Chi confronts his family's organization and later takes up the Ten Rings. Those later rings are comics counterparts to the film's weapons, not their original source; anthology selections open whole issues.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from the owner's selected Comic Book Herald excerpt

lists.name: MCU Prep: Thunderbolts*
lists.description: Meet the comics' Thunderbolts and explore Bucky, Natasha, Yelena and Taskmaster for background on the film's uneasy alliances. The original Thunderbolts arrive as a new team in 1997, while later selections explore Bucky's Winter Soldier past, his own Thunderbolts team and Black Widow's world. This is not the film's exact team or origin. The guide includes all 35 selected originals, including Thunderbolts (1997) #-1 by owner-confirmed identity without inferred provider metadata or availability.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled by hand for this project from the owner-authored outline in GitHub issue #682

lists.name: Moon Knight: MCU Prep
lists.description: Explore Marc Spector's identities and bond with Khonshu for background on Moon Knight's troubled hero. From the Dead, Lunatic and The Midnight Mission offer different approaches to his street-level work, sense of reality and responsibilities. These are distinct comics interpretations, not the show's exact history.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by the owner for MCU Prep; expanded into original issues for this project

lists.name: Eternals
lists.description: Meet the Eternals, Deviants and Celestials in the comics to make sense of the film's ancient cosmic family. The original Eternals run introduces their mythology, the 2006 miniseries explores forgotten identities, and Only Death Is Eternal examines their society. These versions provide background rather than the film's exact history.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: MCU Prep: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
lists.description: Meet the Fantastic Four and read the Galactus Trilogy for the family and cosmic threats behind First Steps. Their earliest adventures introduce the team, Galactus and the Silver Surfer, then later stories deepen the family's scientific curiosity and bonds. New Dawn adds the Silver Surfer's own adventures beyond that first encounter. The Point One selection opens the whole anthology, including stories beyond its Silver Surfer material.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from the owner's selections

lists.name: MCU Prep: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
lists.description: Explore Peter Parker's fresh starts in the comics, including Brand New Day, for background on the film's namesake era. Coming Home, Brand New Day and Back to Basics show different ways of rebuilding Spider-Man's life and responsibilities. This is character context, not a prediction of the film's plot. Venom Super Special (1995) #1 is still missing provider details; the bonus-story selections open their whole original comics.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
lists.description: Meet Jennifer Walters as both lawyer and She-Hulk to understand the superhero legal comedy behind the series. Her first appearance introduces her transformation, while Single Green Female and Law and Disorder explore the collisions between legal work, superhero clients and everyday life.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Ms. Marvel
lists.description: Meet Kamala Khan in her earliest comics to understand the family, fandom and community behind the show's hero. No Normal and Generation Why follow her first steps as a Jersey City superhero, then Destined expands her adventures. Her comics powers and origin differ from the series, and the Point One selection opens the whole anthology.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Captain America: Brave New World
lists.description: Get to know Sam Wilson as Captain America and meet Red Hulk, two comics foundations for Brave New World. Hydra Ascendant and Not My Captain America explore Sam's choices, the shield's legacy and public resistance to his role. The opening Hulk collection introduces Red Hulk in a separate story, not the film's plot.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Guardians of the Galaxy
lists.description: Discover the Guardians' comics formation and unlikely friendships for context on the films' found family. Annihilation: Conquest and Legacy bring the modern team together, followed by Rocket's solo misadventures and a later Guardians lineup. The comics' origins and team history differ from the films.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: MCU Prep: Agatha All Along
lists.description: Meet the comics' Agatha Harkness and explore her tangled bond with Scarlet Witch for context on the show's elusive witch. Her Fantastic Four debut leads into The Last Door and a magical confrontation in Scarlet Witch Annual. The five selected House of Harkness school-rivalry chapters have owner-confirmed identities, while provider details and covers remain unavailable.
lists.sourceOrigin: Selected by raymond-nassar for MCU Prep

lists.name: Agents of Atlas
lists.description: Agents of Atlas from the 1950s background reading through Jeff Parker, Fear Itself, and the New Agents of Atlas.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: MCU Prep: Deadpool & Wolverine
lists.description: Get to know Deadpool's chaotic humor and Wolverine's troubled past before their screen team-up. Weapon X explores Logan's brutal experimentation, while Deadpool's early adventures and Dead Presidents introduce Wade's mercenary world. Gifted adds X-Men context, and Old Man Logan visits an alternate future rather than the film's Wolverine.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from the owner's selections

lists.name: White Tiger: Ava Ayala
lists.description: Ava Ayala, the White Tiger, comes up through Avengers Academy and goes on to stand with the Mighty Avengers and the New Avengers. Christos Gage's Avengers Academy opens it, then Al Ewing's Mighty Avengers, Captain America & the Mighty Avengers and New Avengers. Captain America and Marvel's Voices: Community follow. Only issues featuring Ava are kept from larger collections.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Nova
lists.description: Richard Rider and Sam Alexander both carry the Nova name, at home with the New Warriors and far out in Marvel's cosmic stories. Marv Wolfman's Nova (1976) and Fabian Nicieza's New Warriors (1990) come first. Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning write Annihilation: Nova, Nova (2007) and The Thanos Imperative, and later stops include Nova (2013), Champions (2016) and Guardians of the Galaxy (2019 and 2020).
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Phalanx
lists.description: The Phalanx have roots in the Technarchy of the New Mutants era, and the Phalanx Covenant sweeps across the X-Men books. Chris Claremont's New Mutants comes first, followed by Scott Lobdell's Uncanny X-Men and chapters in X-Factor, X-Force, Excalibur, Wolverine and Cable. Later Uncanny X-Men stories and Si Spurrier's Legion of X close the journey.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Phoenix
lists.description: The Phoenix Force burns through Marvel Comics by way of its hosts, chief among them Jean Grey and Rachel Summers. Chris Claremont's Excalibur leads into Grant Morrison's New X-Men, Jason Aaron's Marvel Legacy and Tom Taylor's X-Men: Red. Jonathan Hickman's X-Men and Louise Simonson's Jean Grey come later. Only picks that identify exact issues are included.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Agatha Harkness
lists.description: Agatha Harkness enters through the Fantastic Four in 1970, and before long her story is tied to the Scarlet Witch and the Vision. Steve Englehart's Avengers and Giant-Size Avengers issues lead to his Vision and the Scarlet Witch (1985), then the West Coast Avengers and Infinity War. Tom King's Vision (2015), James Robinson's Scarlet Witch (2015) and Steve Orlando's Scarlet Witch Annual (2023) come later.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Punisher
lists.description: Frank Castle, the Punisher, works the dark, street-level end of Marvel in crime stories that begin in 1974. The Amazing Spider-Man opens the journey, then Steven Grant's The Punisher, Mike Baron's The Punisher and Carl Potts's Punisher War Journal. Later series include Jason Aaron's Punisher, David Pepose's Punisher and Torunn Gronbekk's War Journal specials. Unmatched originals remain as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Rocket Raccoon
lists.description: Rocket Raccoon from his Half-World debut through the modern Guardians, his solo adventures, and Avengers: No Road Home.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Ultron
lists.description: Ultron's stories pull in the Avengers, Hank Pym, the Vision and Iron Man across fifty years of comics. It moves from the original Avengers to Busiek and Perez's Avengers, Mighty Avengers, Annihilation: Conquest and Rick Remender's Rage of Ultron. The Ultron Agenda in Tony Stark: Iron Man closes it. Avengers #212 to 230 sits after Rage of Ultron, and the animated-continuity Ultron Revolution is included.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Mephisto
lists.description: Mephisto, a Hell Lord, works his way into the stories of the Silver Surfer, Thor, Ghost Rider and Doctor Strange. Jason Aaron's Wolverine opens it before the order goes back to Silver Surfer, Thor, Ghost Rider, the Defenders, Al Milgrom's Mephisto Vs. and the graphic novel Triumph and Torment. One More Day and Damnation follow, and Aaron's Avengers ends it. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Spider-Man 2099
lists.description: Miguel O'Hara is the Spider-Man of 2099, and his story runs through the 2099 line and out into Exiles, Spider-Verse and beyond. Peter David writes Spider-Man 2099 and returns for later series and Secret Wars 2099, with Exiles and Timestorm 2009/2099 in between. Steve Orlando's Exodus, Dark Genesis and Miguel O'Hara: Spider-Man 2099 close it. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Silver Surfer
lists.description: Norrin Radd, the Silver Surfer, arrives with Galactus in 1966, and from there his stories range across Marvel's cosmos. Fantastic Four leads to the Defenders, Steve Englehart's Silver Surfer, Jim Starlin's Infinity Gauntlet and J. Michael Straczynski's Requiem. Dan Slott's Silver Surfer, Donny Cates's Black and Ron Marz's Rebirth books come later.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Abomination
lists.description: The Abomination belongs to the Hulk's corner of Marvel, and nearly every stop on this journey is a Hulk story. It opens in Tales to Astonish, and most of it sits in Incredible Hulk, with writers from Roy Thomas and Bill Mantlo to Peter David. There are stops in Thor, Avengers, Amazing Spider-Man and X-Men too. Later appearances named only in passing are left out.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Defenders
lists.description: Doctor Strange, the Hulk, Namor and the Silver Surfer come together as the Defenders, a team that starts out as no team at all. Roy Thomas's Sub-Mariner and Marvel Feature lead into Defenders, where Steve Englehart, Steve Gerber and J. M. DeMatteis write long stretches. Later lineups follow in Secret Defenders, The Last Defenders, Fearless Defenders and Al Ewing's Defenders.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Runaways
lists.description: The Runaways grow up on the page in a coming-of-age story that later crosses paths with the Young Avengers. Brian K. Vaughan's Runaways opens the journey, and Vaughan and Joss Whedon continue in the later series. Young Avengers crossovers lead to Runaways stories by Terry Moore, Noelle Stevenson and Rainbow Rowell.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Adam Warlock
lists.description: Adam Warlock begins as Him and becomes a cosmic figure bound up with Thanos, Gamora and the Infinity Gauntlet. Fantastic Four and Thor come first, then Roy Thomas's Marvel Premiere and Jim Starlin's Strange Tales and Warlock. Starlin returns for Thanos Quest, Infinity Gauntlet, the Infinity Watch and Infinity War, and The Thanos Imperative and Thanos Annual come late.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Black Panther
lists.description: T'Challa is the Black Panther of Wakanda, first met in the Fantastic Four and then the lead of series after series of his own. Fantastic Four opens the journey, followed by Don McGregor's Jungle Action and the 1977 Black Panther series. Christopher Priest, Reginald Hudlin, Ta-Nehisi Coates, John Ridley and Eve Ewing each write later series, with Nnedi Okorafor's Shuri along the way.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Groot
lists.description: Groot from his first appearance through the modern Guardians, solo adventures, Rocket partnership, and his 2023 origin series.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Silk / Cindy Moon
lists.description: Cindy Moon becomes Silk, a hero from Spider-Man's corner of Marvel who also finds a place with the Agents of Atlas. Dan Slott's Amazing Spider-Man opens the journey, followed by Robbie Thompson's Silk and the Spider-Women crossover. Greg Pak's Totally Awesome Hulk and Agents of Atlas and Maurene Goo's Silk are also here. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Spider-Gwen / Ghost-Spider
lists.description: Gwen Stacy goes by Spider-Gwen and later Ghost-Spider, and her story is full of crossovers with other spider-heroes. Edge of Spider-Verse and Spider-Verse open the journey, then Jason Latour's Spider-Gwen, with the Spider-Women crossover and Spider-Geddon to follow. Seanan McGuire's Ghost-Spider books, Tim Seeley's Gwenverse and Emily Kim's Shadow Clones come later. The unnumbered Gwenom vs Carnage collection is not expanded.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Star-Lord
lists.description: Peter Quill from his earliest cosmic adventures through the Guardians, solo series, and Old Man Quill.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Iron Man
lists.description: Tony Stark is Iron Man, and his story makes room over the years for War Machine and Ironheart as well. It begins in Tales of Suspense in 1963 and runs to the modern Invincible Iron Man, Tony Stark: Iron Man and Iron Man (2020), with Armor Wars and Extremis among the stories along the way. Where a larger collection only touches Iron Man, just his issues are kept.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Modern X-Men Fast Track
lists.description: Cyclops, Wolverine, Jean Grey and the rest of the X-Men carry this modern stretch, from Grant Morrison to Brian Michael Bendis. New X-Men (2001) opens it, then Peter Milligan's X-Force and X-Statix, Astonishing X-Men from Joss Whedon and Warren Ellis, Mike Carey's X-Men Legacy and Matt Fraction's Uncanny X-Men. Bendis's All-New X-Men comes at the end. Linked events and collection-only references are left out.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Thanos
lists.description: Thanos starts with the Cosmic Cube campaigns of the 1970s, and his stories keep running into those of Adam Warlock and the Silver Surfer. Iron Man and Captain Marvel come first, then Jim Starlin's Strange Tales, Warlock, Silver Surfer, Thanos Quest, Infinity War and Infinity Crusade. Donny Cates's Cosmic Ghost Rider and Tini Howard's Thanos come later, and Thor closes it. Entries without provider details are retained.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Ant-Man
lists.description: Ant-Man from Hank Pym’s first appearance through Scott Lang, Eric O’Grady, and the modern Ant-Man and the Wasp era.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Bucky Barnes / Winter Soldier
lists.description: Bucky Barnes first stands beside Captain America in 1941, and later his story turns to dark espionage thrillers as the Winter Soldier. Captain America Comics and All-Winners Comics lead to Roy Thomas's Invaders, then Ed Brubaker's Captain America. Later stops include Invaders, Falcon & Winter Soldier, Thunderbolts and Kyle Higgins's Winter Soldier. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Wolverine
lists.description: Wolverine's story runs on two tracks at once, with the X-Men and in solo books of his own, and later in Old Man Logan. Giant-Size X-Men and Uncanny X-Men begin the journey, followed by Chris Claremont's Wolverine and Kitty Pryde and Wolverine. Old Man Logan and Dead Man Logan close it. Unmatched originals remain as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Hope Summers
lists.description: Called the Mutant Messiah, Hope Summers is at the heart of Messiah Complex and Second Coming, and later of Generation Hope and Krakoa. Messiah Complex runs through books by Ed Brubaker, Peter David, Christopher Yost and Mike Carey, and Duane Swierczynski's Cable follows. After Second Coming the journey reaches Kieron Gillen's Immortal X-Men. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Hulk (and She-Hulk, Red Hulk)
lists.description: The Hulk's world keeps growing, until She-Hulk, Red Hulk and Skaar each carry stories of their own beside his. The original Incredible Hulk opens the journey, then Tales to Astonish, The Savage She-Hulk and long Incredible Hulk stretches credited to Roy Thomas, Steve Englehart, Bill Mantlo and Peter David. It reaches Incredible Hulk, Imperial and its Imperial War specials.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Black Widow
lists.description: As the Black Widow, Natasha Romanoff turns up among the Avengers and in long stretches of Daredevil before leading series of her own. It begins in Tales of Suspense and takes in Amazing Adventures, Daredevil from Gerry Conway to Frank Miller, the Champions and the West Coast Avengers. Late stops include Jen and Sylvia Soska's Black Widow, Jody Houser's The Web of Black Widow and Kelly Thompson's Black Widow.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Daredevil
lists.description: The complete Daredevil guide, from the character origins through modern runs and team ups.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Iron Fist
lists.description: Danny Rand fights as the Iron Fist, sharing his story with Luke Cage, Colleen Wing and Misty Knight along the way. Marvel Premiere and Chris Claremont's Iron Fist open the journey, followed by Power Man and Iron Fist and John Ostrander's Heroes for Hire. Immortal Iron Fist comes later, and Larry Hama's Heart of the Dragon and Alyssa Wong's Iron Fist close it. Unresolved originals remain marked as gaps.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Ultimate Spider-Man
lists.description: Peter Parker and Miles Morales are Spider-Man in Marvel's Ultimate universes, the original one and a separate new one. Brian Michael Bendis's Ultimate Spider-Man opens the journey alongside Ultimate Marvel Team-Up, Ultimate Six and Ultimatum. Ultimate Comics Spider-Man and Spider-Men follow, and Jonathan Hickman's Ultimate Spider-Man leads into Ultimate Endgame.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Venom
lists.description: Out of the 1984 Secret Wars comes a black costume that goes on to bond with host after host for decades. Secret Wars and Spider-Man's black costume saga lead to Eddie Brock in David Michelinie's Lethal Protector, followed by the Donny Cates and Al Ewing years. Most of the closing 2025 and 2026 entries, Queen in Black among them, have no details, covers or Unlimited links.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Loki
lists.description: Before Loki ever carries a series of his own, his story runs for years through Thor's world in Journey Into Mystery and Thor. Later comes Rob Rodi's Loki, Walt Simonson's Thor, Kieron Gillen's Thor stories, War of the Realms, Daniel Kibblesmith's Loki and Mariko Tamaki's Thor & Loki: Double Trouble, ending with Dan Watters' Loki.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Moon Knight
lists.description: Moon Knight from his Werewolf by Night debut through his modern solo runs, Avengers appearances, and latest collected adventures.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Guardians of the Galaxy
lists.description: For over fifty years the Guardians of the Galaxy name passes from revival to revival, each one rebuilt for a new space epic. Marvel Super-Heroes begins the journey, followed by Jim Valentino and Michael Gallagher's 1990 series and the 2008 relaunch by Abnett and Lanning. Bendis, Donny Cates, Al Ewing, and Kelly and Lanzing carry it to 2023, with Black Vortex along the way.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Doctor Strange
lists.description: Mystic battles fill six decades, starting with Strange Tales and reaching the Sorcerer Supreme's 2023 series. Along the way come the Defenders, the 1970s Doctor Strange series and Strange Academy by Skottie Young. It closes with Jed MacKay's Doctor Strange.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Inhumans
lists.description: When the Fantastic Four first meet them in 1965, the Inhumans and their royal family are drawn into decades of war and cosmic politics. Fantastic Four and Paul Jenkins's Inhumans lead to Son of M, Silent War, War of Kings and Realm of Kings. Infinity, Inhumanity, Charles Soule's Inhuman titles, Al Ewing's Royals and Saladin Ahmed's Black Bolt carry the journey to 2018.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Young Avengers
lists.description: In 2005 young heroes take up the Avengers name, and their story spreads through team books and solo series for nearly two decades. Allan Heinberg's Children's Crusade and Kieron Gillen's Young Avengers follow the original series. Kate Bishop appears in Kelly Thompson's Hawkeye, while West Coast Avengers, Hulkling & Wiccan and Gabby Rivera's America add more stories. Death's Head: Clone Drive is a placeholder.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Magneto
lists.description: Magneto is there from the earliest Uncanny X-Men issues, and the decades that follow bring event series and solo books of his own. It runs through the Claremont-era Uncanny X-Men, Leah Williams' X-Men: The Trial of Magneto, Al Ewing's X-Men Red and J.M. DeMatteis' Magneto, closing with an Al Ewing series. Unresolved entries stay as plain-text provenance, and a placeholder remains.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Apocalypse / X-Men: Age of Apocalypse
lists.description: In 1995 the X-books give way to replacement titles set in the Age of Apocalypse, and later series keep returning to that world. Legion Quest leads to X-Men: Alpha and titles such as Generation Next, Gambit and the X-Ternals, Weapon X, X-Man and Amazing X-Men. Blink and Remender's Uncanny Avengers follow, then X-Men: Heir of Apocalypse. Later entries are placeholders.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: X-Men Core Reading Order: Silver Age to Claremont
lists.description: Before Fall of the Mutants and Inferno, the X-Men grow from the first class into Chris Claremont's sprawling cast. Giant-Size X-Men, the Claremont years, Phoenix, Dark Phoenix, the Brood, Days of Future Past, God Loves Man Kills, New Mutants and Louise Simonson's X-Factor follow. X-Men #67 to 93 are skipped as reprints, and the Mutant Massacre is read interleaved.
lists.variant: The spine, without the optional reading
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: X-Men Expanded Reading Order: Silver Age to Claremont
lists.description: The expanded Silver Age-to-Claremont route adds the two sections the outline marked optional to the core reading order. Compiled by hand from the same reader's outline of Comic Book Herald's guides. The Silver Age add-ons are the guest appearances that carried the X-Men through the years their own title was running reprints, scattered across Amazing Adventures, Spider-Man, the Hulk, the Avengers, Captain America, the Defenders and Giant-Size Fantastic Four. The modern retellings revisit the same years from the outside: The Hidden Years, Grand Design, Season One and the whole of First Class. X-Men Annual #1 and #2 are listed without a link, because Marvel's metadata carries that series only from #3.
lists.variant: With the optional add-ons and retellings
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project

lists.name: Shadow King
lists.description: Professor X's clashes with Amahl Farouk, the Shadow King, keep resurfacing across decades of X-books. Chris Claremont's Uncanny X-Men begins the journey, and later chapters come in New Excalibur, Rick Remender's Uncanny X-Force, Charles Soule's Astonishing X-Men and Vita Ayala's Age of X-Man: Prisoner X. The Muir Island stories are interleaved, and Ayala's New Mutants closes it.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Professor X (Charles Xavier)
lists.description: Long before Krakoa, Charles Xavier's story runs from the Silver Age through the Claremont years and Morrison and Quitely's New X-Men. Deadly Genesis, the Rise and Fall of the Shi'ar Empire, New Avengers: Illuminati and X-Men: Legacy run to 2009. Onslaught, Krakoa and the 2024 finale continue on the Professor X and the X-Men path in Modern Timeline. In memory of Sir Patrick Stewart (1940 to 2026), who brought Professor X to life on screen.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Captain Marvel / Ms. Marvel
lists.description: A source-defined Captain Marvel / Ms. Marvel guide with exact issue links from Mar-Vell through Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau, and the modern Captain Marvel runs.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Ms. Marvel (Kamala Khan)
lists.description: In her first decade as a hero, Kamala Khan carries her own series while joining the Avengers, the Champions and other teams. G. Willow Wilson's Ms. Marvel leads to Saladin Ahmed's Magnificent Ms. Marvel, with All-New, All-Different Avengers, Champions, Marvel Rising and Dark Web alongside. Some entries are placeholders.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Best of Captain America
lists.description: Deliberately out of publication order, this opens in Ed Brubaker's spy-thriller years and later doubles back to the Red Skull's classics. Brubaker's Captain America leads through Reborn and Rebirth to Man Out of Time by Mark Waid. Captain America and Bucky follows, then Tales of Suspense, The Life and Times of the Red Skull and Gruenwald's The Captain.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Captain America: Modern Marvel Era
lists.description: This modern-era stretch with Steve Rogers, Sam Wilson, Bucky Barnes, Sharon Carter and the Red Skull is mostly kept as provenance. Captain America (2004) #25 is the resolved issue; the collection and range entries around it are retained rather than guessed at, including the run toward Secret Empire.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: There is Only Doom
lists.description: Doom's legend is built here in layers: his origin and its retellings, his sieges of the Fantastic Four, and his bids for cosmic power. It moves from Fantastic Four to the Ultimate retelling, Books of Doom and Werner von Doom. Doomquest in Iron Man, the Silver Surfer and the Power Cosmic, Secret Wars, Infinity Gauntlet and Infamous Iron Man follow.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: 10 Best Spider-Man (Peter Parker) Comics Reading List
lists.description: Across half a century of Peter Parker's life, these selections pick out standout stories, beginning with the Lee and Ditko origins. The Hobgoblin, the Jean DeWolff story, Kraven's Last Hunt, Harry Osborn, Straczynski's Coming Home, the Gauntlet and Slott's Superior Spider-Man lead to Life Story. Amazing Spider-Man #600, #606 and #611 and the Big Time issues #648 to 652 are optional preludes.
lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: The Best of Thor

lists.name: Ultimate Marvel: Intro to the Ultimate U

lists.name: Marvel 2099
lists.description: An alternate universe set in the year 2099 has its own Spider-Man, Doom, X-Men and Ghost Rider, launched in the early 1990s. lists.name: Maximum Security

lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Falcon / Sam Wilson / Captain America

lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Fantastic Four
lists.description: Since November 1961 Reed Richards, Sue and Johnny Storm and Ben Grimm have carried the Fantastic Four, and their adventures run into 2025. lists.sourceOrigin: Compiled for this project from Comic Book Herald's guide

lists.name: Nick Fury and S.H.I.E.L.D.

Fury, written by Stan Lee and then Roy Thomas, with Gary Friedrich also credited, alongside Marvel Spotlight and Jonathan Hickman's S.H.I.E.L.D. lists.name: Power Pack: Pack Attack! and Team-Ups
lists.description: With alien-given powers, the young Power siblings spend years teaming up with one Marvel hero after another. Marc Sumerak's Pack Attack! reboot leads to team-ups with the X-Men, Avengers, Spider-Man, Hulk, Fantastic Four and Iron Man, then Fred Van Lente's Day One origin and Skrulls Vs. Power Pack. Wolverine and Power Pack and Thor and the Warriors Four close the journey.
